proofRule.decision: D13 (user, 2026-09-06): none means NO TELEMETRY EMITTED, not no instrumentation loaded. not-loaded and loaded-silenced both satisfy disabledService; only loaded-exporting blocks a posture. The loaded-silenced services keep running instrumentation code and keep costing, and that residual cost is carried as postureRealization.claimBoundary, not as a blocker.

disabledLoadStateVocabulary.not-loaded: The disabled posture never loads the instrumentation agent, SDK, module, or autoloader; the process starts through the plain entrypoint with no instrumentation code path. This is the strongest state that satisfies proofRule.disabledService, and the only one that also removes the residual instrumentation cost.
disabledLoadStateVocabulary.loaded-silenced: Instrumentation code is compiled or imported into the process, but a source-verified SDK switch makes it a no-op and it exports nothing; residual instrumentation work remains, so a cost baseline is still perturbed. Under D13 this satisfies proofRule.disabledService (nothing is emitted) and is reported as postureRealization.claimBoundary; it is NOT a claim that the instrumentation is absent.
disabledLoadStateVocabulary.loaded-exporting: Instrumentation code is compiled into the process and the pinned SDK honours neither OTEL_SDK_DISABLED nor OTEL_*_EXPORTER=none; the service exports telemetry in every posture and structurally breaks the disabled posture.

none.rule: no application service may emit telemetry: every service must reach disabledLoadState not-loaded or loaded-silenced (D13)
